title: Heapfold KV allocation strategy and live defragmentation for continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: introduce a 'Heapfold' allocation strategy and an accompanying lightweight live-defragmentation subsystem to reduce long-term KV cache fragmentation and tail latencies in continuous batching workloads without increasing per-request CPU overhead or breaking KV cache semantics. The design blends a small fixed-slab tier for hot short-lived entries with a compacting heap tier for variable-length KV values and a background micro-migration process coordinated with batching windows and kernel occupancy. This reduces memory waste from partially filled slabs and avoids large pause events by migrating small groups of entries incrementally during low-GPU-occupancy micro-windows.
tasks: Proto: implement Heapfold allocator abstraction (slab tier + compacting heap tier) in runtime alloc module
Telemetry: emit per-pool occupancy, frag ratio, live-migration latency, and batch-alignment delta metrics
Defrag: implement micro-migrate worker with batch-coordinated pacing and soft-throttle
Routing: integrate with scheduler to prefer packing new KV entries into slab tier when expected TTL < threshold
Eviction: add generational eviction hinting to avoid migrating imminently-evicted entries
Benchmarks: run mixed-length token generation microbench across seq-len distributions and batch sizes
Rollout: implement feature-flagged canary with runtime knob for migration aggressiveness
acceptance_criteria: Production build exposes Heapfold behind feature flag and runtime knobs
Observed fragmentation (bytes wasted / allocated) reduced by >=30% on mixed workload compared to baseline in canary cluster
P95 tail token-latency does not regress by more than 5% during steady-state continuous batching
Live-migration worker keeps per-GPU CPU utilization increase < 6% and memory copy overhead amortized across batches
No correctness regressions: KV lookup and cache hits remain stable; canary tests validate cache invariants
comments: 2025-01-12 - Asha Patel: Initial triage and writeup. Identified that frequent small allocations from tokenized KV entries are causing slab internal waste when token lengths vary. Proposed hybrid slab+heap approach (Heapfold) to consolidate fragments.

2025-01-20 - Miguel Ramirez: Spike complete. Proto allocator implemented with simple bump-heap backed by a free-list. Basic migration flow works but caused a brief 200ms GPU stall when mass-copying >4MB groups. Need batch-coordinated pacing.

2025-01-25 - Priya Singh (PM): Design review feedback: prioritize predictable tail latency and make migration aggressiveness configurable per-customer. Add explicit rollout plan and observability dashboard.
2025-01-30 - Design review (Liam O'Connor): UX note: expose a single 'fragmentation_tolerance' knob rather than separate thresholds to avoid config complexity for teams using Dedicated capacity.
2025-02-05 - Miguel Ramirez: Implemented batch-aligned micro-windows. Migration now copies groups sized to fit in next N batches (default N=3). Tail stall reduced in internal perf runs.

2025-02-10 - QA (Eve Zhang): Canary run started on two nodes. Initial metrics show 34% avg reduction in wasted KB and 3% p95 latency improvement for small-token workload. Observed slight increase in CPU spin during peak—tuning migration pacing next.

2025-02-14 - Security (Rajiv Kumar): Reviewed data movement mechanism. No OS-level page protections violated. Recommended adding a telemetry tag for customer_data_class to gate higher-sensitivity customers from aggressive migration. Marked as note in rollout checklist.

2025-02-15 - Miguel Ramirez: Opened PR 3876 with allocator refactor and migration worker. Requesting eng review and perf validation on dedicated cluster. Next: add generational eviction and adjustable migration window based on measured TTL distribution. Blocker: need updated kernel copy path to avoid memcopy fallback on older GPUs. Raised infra ticket to update driver stack.
